component.name: runetty
component.summary: Manage SSH sessions, long-running jobs and server health

description.p: runetty puts three things most people juggle across terminal tabs into a single native window: SSH sessions, the long-running jobs on each server, and how those servers are doing.

It builds on the SSH setup you already have. Hosts come straight from ~/.ssh/config, which runetty only ever reads. Nothing is installed on the far side: monitoring reads /proc, and jobs are plain tmux sessions. If a server accepts ssh, it works.

ul.li: Tabbed terminals, with the shell keybindings left alone
Sidebar with folders, drag and drop, filtering and recent hosts
Host key fingerprints shown for approval, never auto-accepted
Passwords kept in the system keyring, never in a file
Per-host monitoring: CPU, memory, disks, network and top processes
Long-running tmux sessions listed as agents, with one click to attach
Command palette, full keyboard shortcut reference, light and dark themes

screenshot.caption: Terminal sessions with the server sidebar
Long-running tmux sessions listed as agents

description.p: The application ID is now io.github.umutcanpurtul_avi.runetty, which is how Flathub verifies ownership without a domain name. A Flatpak installed under the old ID should be removed and reinstalled; your records and saved passwords are kept.

Adds a command palette over servers and commands, and tightens the handling of secrets: unrecognised ssh prompts are refused rather than answered with a password, ~/.ssh is created privately, and the record files are no longer world-readable.
First release. SSH sessions with tabs, records from ~/.ssh/config and the app's own store, host key approval, passwords in the system keyring, live host monitoring, and tmux sessions as agents.
